Subject: Big news from the trenches: Fernhollow Photo is real!

Okay, deep breath. I have some big news, and I wanted to tell you all here before I try to say it out loud over Thanksgiving dinner with a plate of stuffing in one hand.

I’m officially on my own. Fernhollow Photo is a real business now!!

Rosebud Lane closed at the end of October, and after four years of shooting for Marisol, I’m starting the next chapter as a wedding photographer under my own name. Marisol taught me so much over those four years, and I’m incredibly grateful for her. She’s been cheering me on and referring couples my way, and I wouldn’t be where I am without her. She deserves a huge shoutout for being a wonderful mentor.

I know “starting a business” can sound like I woke up one morning, bought a new camera, and decided to see what happens. That is not what happened! I’ve been thinking and planning this in my head for two years. I’m excited, and yes, a little scared too, because apparently big life choices come with a side of butterflies. But I have a plan, I’ve been working at it, and I’m ready to give it a real go.

Here are some actual numbers, because I know some of you will ask: I have 14 weddings booked for 2027 already. Six couples came to me through Marisol, and eight found me on my own. I’m so thankful to Marisol for the referrals, and also very proud that people are finding my work independently. My website went live this month, and I’ve already got a calendar full of people trusting me with one of their biggest days. That is a lot to take in, in the best way.

And I got my first booking that was 100% mine! Dahlia and Ken are getting married at Timberline on June 12. They found me because of the Multnomah Falls couple photos I took, and they chose me for their wedding. I read their email and immediately did that thing where you stare at the screen to make sure it’s real. Then I texted Sam. Then I probably stared at the screen again.

For the larger weddings, Jae will second shoot with me. Jae is great, and I’m happy to have another talented human there to help catch all the moments happening at once. Jae will be paid per wedding, because this is a business and good work deserves to be paid. (Also, two photographers means a better chance of catching both the first kiss and whoever is making a very emotional face in the front row.)

A little explanation of the name, especially for Grandma: Fernhollow is from the fern hollow trail behind your old place in Gresham. That’s where I took my first real pictures with your Pentax. I can still remember carrying it around and feeling like I’d found a whole new way to notice things. I wanted the name to hold onto that beginning, and to feel like the kind of place I’d want to take people’s photographs. Grandma, this one’s for you. Thank you for letting me borrow that camera and for being part of where all this started.

The business paperwork was less picturesque. I filed the LLC on my lunch break in the car outside Fred Meyer and cried a little. Not a dramatic movie cry, exactly. More of a “well, I really did it” cry, followed by going back to work and trying to act normal. Fernhollow Photo LLC is official, which is a very serious sentence for something I started while parked in a grocery store lot.

Sam has been very supportive through all of this, including the extremely important cake portion of the process. He made a cake that said FERNHOLOW, with one L missing. We ate it anyway. It was delicious, and frankly, the spelling error makes it a limited-edition business launch cake.

One practical thing before Dad has to ask: I have health insurance sorted. I picked a marketplace plan, and it starts January 1. I’ve got that handled, Dad. You can save the health insurance speech for another day—or skip it entirely and just ask me how the weddings are going. I know you care, and I appreciate that. I promise I’m taking the practical parts seriously, too.

I really wanted you all to hear this from me before Thanksgiving, because it’s exciting and a little vulnerable to put it out there. I’m not expecting anybody to solve it for me; I just want to share this big thing with the people I love. There will be plenty to learn as I go, and I’m sure there will be long days and camera gear drama and at least one more cake spelling incident. But I’m proud of the work I’ve done, and I’m excited about what comes next.

Also, if anybody wants free family pictures at Thanksgiving, I’ll bring the camera! No pressure and no coordinated outfits required. I will photograph you as you are, including Uncle Greg pretending he isn’t cold and whoever gets caught going back for a third roll.

Love you all. I’ll see you at Ruthie’s, and I’m bringing the rolls, the cranberry thing, and probably a camera.
